review_notes: I read the whole target file. I then read the related rank-fiber definitions in Module/RankFiberDecomposition.lean (rankFiberModule, rankFiberRingEquiv, rankFiberLinearEquiv) and the local block in ExteriorPower/DeterminantLine.lean (lines ~851-867). The main proof in the target is long but mostly a single linear argument. The only repeated machinery I found is the "product-of-rings decomposition of a module" equivalence, which is written out about five times across these files. This is a def-level composite of three standard equivalences and not deep reasoning, so the finding is moderate. I have not compiled the proposed helper. Its instance and universe requirements (Fintype and DecidableEq on the index, `classical`) mirror the existing uses, but they are unchecked. I found no other repeated blocks.

findings.problem: dX and dY are the same three-step construction applied to X and Y. The steps are `lid.symm`, then `AlgebraTensorModule.congr` along the ring decomposition `rankFiberRingEquiv`, then `TensorProduct.piLeft`. The identical recipe is also written out in `Module.rankFiberLinearEquiv` (RankFiberDecomposition.lean, which does it for N = M) and twice more as `sourceEquiv` and `targetEquiv` in DeterminantLine.lean. That is about five copies of one 'decompose any module along a ring-product splitting R ≃ₐ ∀ t, S t' construction. Each copy repeats the long index and ring type ascription. A change to the decomposition, for example to its instance arguments, has to be made in every copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general helper next to `rankFiberLinearEquiv`, or in a TensorProduct utilities file. Its statement is: for `e : R ≃ₐ[R] ∀ t, S t` (with `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` on the index) and any `R`-module `N`, define `piDecomp e N : N ≃ₗ[R] ∀ t, S t ⊗[R] N := (TensorProduct.lid R N).symm ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr e.toLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.refl R N) ≪≫ₗ TensorProduct.piLeft R N S`. Then specialise it once for rank fibers: `Module.rankFiberDecomp R M N := piDecomp (rankFiberRingEquiv R M) N`. Under their actual hypotheses the uses become:
- `rankFiberLinearEquiv R M := rankFiberDecomp R M M`.
- In the target, `dX := Module.rankFiberDecomp B Q X` and `dY := Module.rankFiberDecomp B Q Y`, with the two 7-line `let`s deleted. Here R = B, N = X or Y and the ring is `rankFiberRingEquiv B Q`, so the types match the ascribed `∀ j, rankFiberRing B Q j ⊗[B] X`.
- In DeterminantLine.lean, `sourceEquiv := piDecomp ringEquiv (DeterminantLine R P ⊗[R] DeterminantLine R Q)` and `targetEquiv := piDecomp ringEquiv (DeterminantLine R (P × Q))`.
No new mathematics is needed, because the helper body is the existing term abstracted over `N`. Extensionality or compatibility facts about the pieces can then be proved once, if they are ever needed.
findings.benefit: It removes about 30 duplicated lines across three files, and the main proof of `determinantLine_mk` gets shorter. The role of dX and dY ('same partition of the spectrum, applied to X and Y') becomes visible from the names. Any future change to the decomposition, such as instance arguments or a switch to `Pi.ringEquiv`, is made in one place instead of five.
